Lock ordering, interrupt context and lifetime rules beyond mutex and sleepable guard uses shown.
Full ELF header, program header and note record layouts and numeric ABI values.
Non empty device RAM processing, callback registration and device dump production paths.

findings.text: Callback unregistration is externally visible and detaches a callback object from the global callback list under mutex protection, warns once if removal happens after the vmcore file was opened, and then waits for preexisting readers to drain.

Old crash memory read is externally visible and transfers a requested byte count from a given position across page boundaries, emitting zeros for pages classified as non RAM and otherwise using a page copy path selected by an encryption flag, with short transfers reported as faults.

Core header allocation and release, header and note reads, old memory remap and encrypted old memory page copy have weak default implementations that succeed trivially, do nothing, forward to generic old memory read or generic remap behavior, and exist for platform override.
Total vmcore image size is the sum of header area size plus note area size plus the sizes of all memory ranges on the global range list.
Range file offsets form a contiguous sequence in list order beginning immediately after the header and note areas, each offset advancing by the size of the preceding range.

Header buffer capacity is page rounded and never shrinks; a larger request keeps the existing allocation when its allocation order is unchanged and otherwise allocates a new zeroed store, preserves old contents, releases the old store and records the new capacity.

Extension of the program header table for device RAM ranges is refused when the resulting header count would exceed the ELF half count width, and on success header count, buffer size, range list membership, program header offsets and total image size are mutually consistent.

After header table changes the note program header if present is anchored at the end of the header area while other program headers preserve intra page displacement and are repacked contiguously on page granularity after header plus note areas, with range offsets recomputed consistently.

Note consolidation reduces all note program headers to one note program header, shrinks the header area by the removed entries, page rounds the result, updates the header count accordingly and records the unrounded combined note payload size for later device dump accounting.

Per note program header payload size is recomputed by walking note records until a zero name length terminator, accumulating record header plus padded name and descriptor lengths, stopping with a warning if declared capacity would be exceeded and warning when no records are found.

Page classification defaults to RAM and consults registered callbacks that supply a classifier; negative classification makes read paths emit zeros and remap paths substitute the shared zero page for affected pages while preserving surrounding contiguous mappings.
Within the note area device dump payload precedes ordinary note payload so unused tail space does not appear between records, and both copy and map paths honor that partition.
Note buffer allocation uses a user mappable virtual allocation when address translation management is present and a zeroed virtual allocation otherwise.
One build of the device RAM processing hook performs no action.
A global mutex serializes callback list mutation, the sticky opened indicator and the open reference count across unregister, open and release.

A sleepable read side guard protects callback list traversal while classifying pages, copying old memory and selecting the remap path, with a grace wait after unregistration so removed callbacks are no longer referenced.

A memory range node carries a physical start, a byte length, a computed file offset and list linkage, and is the unit for size summation, offset assignment and translation between file position and old memory address.
A device dump node carries a buffer pointer, a byte length and list linkage, and is consumed as a concatenated byte stream addressed by a running offset for both copy and map paths.
A callback object carries list linkage and an optional page classifier hook; absent hooks are skipped and iteration stops at the first negative classification.
Vmcore open state combines a sticky opened flag set on first open with a reference count incremented on open and decremented on release, where increment wrap is rejected as busy.

The readable image is partitioned into header area, device dump prefix plus remaining notes, and memory ranges; reads are bounded by total size, fill the caller iterator across partitions in file order, return accumulated length when the iterator fills, and yield the processor during long scans.
The mappable image follows the same partition order with cumulative mapped length accounting; failure after partial progress unmaps only the completed prefix and reports a retryable mapping failure.
The proc operations object binds open, release, iterated read, default seek and mmap handlers for the vmcore file.
The vmcore page fault operation has two builds: one resolving file offsets through the read path into cached up to date pages, and one unconditionally reporting a bus error.

Mmap entry rejects mappings extending past total image size and rejects writable or executable requests, adjusts mapping flags to mixed without write or execute may permissions, and installs the vmcore fault operations before mapping any partition.
Short iterator copies, short old memory transfers and mapping helper failures surface as fault failures, while note payload reads propagate underlying read failures.

Table extension, allocation, shrink, counter wrap, permission and mapping failures surface as distinct no space, no memory, invalid argument, busy, permission, not implemented and retryable mapping errors, with partial mmap progress rolled back and misaligned device ranges recorded as one time warnings.

Interoperability rests on ELF header program count and program header type, offset and memory size fields plus note record name and descriptor lengths, with a dedicated note type selecting note headers and load entries added for device RAM ranges.
Header, note and payload file offsets and sizes participating in mapping and offset recomputation are expressed and rounded on platform page granularity.
